Until now, article 108 establishes that the president can only be tried during the time of his mandate for treason and serious crimes of the common order. This procedural immunity is also used by other public officials, such as senators and deputies. The jurisdiction is based on the argument that during their office, the president and legislators are obliged to dedicate themselves to providing care to the Mexican people, so they cannot be prosecuted or detained. The president of Mexico, Andrés Manuel López Obrador, has achieved one of his first campaign promises. The Executive published this Friday in the Official Gazette of the Federation (DOF) the decree that reforms articles 108 and 111 of the Constitution on the elimination of presidential jurisdiction. The modifications, previously endorsed by the Chambers of Deputies and Senators as well as by the state Congresses, contemplate that "during the time of his office, the president may be charged and tried for treason, acts of corruption, electoral crimes and all those crimes for which a citizen could be prosecuted." López Noriega added that although the modification to article 108 establishes that the president may be prosecuted like any citizen, article 111 maintains the requirement that said accusation must have the endorsement of two-thirds of the Senate, a prerogative that the rest of the people do not have. “The political protection lock remains,” he concluded. For the expert, beyond the possibility that the president's procedural protection could be removed, the most pressing priority of the Mexican justice system must be the strengthening of the country's prosecutors' offices.

The myth circulates that all products with the 750 prefix are 100% Mexican, but this is false. This error originated from Donald Trump's statements about trade with Mexico, and spread quickly through social networks. GS1 Mexico, in charge of barcodes in the country, has clarified that the prefix only means that the product was registered in Mexico, but not necessarily that the company is Mexican. Even when they manage to enter the labor market, women face worse working conditions. They are more exposed to unemployment (11%), demanding underemployment (13%) and labor informality (36%) than men (8%, 9% and 31%, respectively) (EPH, 1st 2018). Women are more likely to be excluded from the labor market, particularly when they belong to the lowest income quintiles, have children under 6 years old, achieve lower educational levels, and are younger. The flip side of this situation is the time they dedicate to unpaid work and caring for other people at home. Almost twice as many women care as men, and they dedicate 2 hours more per day than men to this task (6 versus 4) (EAHU, 2013). Women face “glass walls”: they participate more in the least dynamic and lowest paid sectors of the economy. 6 out of 10 women work in domestic service, commerce, education and health, while 6 out of 10 of them do so in commerce, construction, industry and in business, real estate and rental activities (EPH, 1st 2018). Introduction: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) caused by the novel coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) has rapidly posed a medical emergency and global crisis since it first emerged in December 2019. On March 11, 2020, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared a pandemic. COVID-19 vaccines are now critical players in the global SARS-CoV-2 situation, with the goal of progressively achieving herd immunity. The WHO has approved 9 vaccines between December 30, 2020 and December 20, 2021. 
Objective: the objective of this study is to analyze, from the contributions made by Biotechnology, the different vaccines that are being administered, as well as those that are in research and development, for the prevention of COVID-19. 
Materials and methods 
An exhaustive review of the literature dedicated to vaccines approved or in clinical instances intended for the prevention of COVID-19 was carried out.  Keywords: COVID-19, SARS-CoV-2, vaccines, biotechnology, vectors, and coronavirus; in the databases MEDLINE/Pubmed, Scielo (Scientific Electronic Library Online), Nature, Lancet and Google Scholar. Inclusion criteria for scientific works: i) English or Spanish language, ii) published between 2019-2021, iii) referring to Biotechnology. Exclusion criteria: i) conventional drugs/vaccines not approved or recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) or the Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) for use in the disease caused by COVID-19. Then, the findings of the selected articles were described qualitatively. 
Results: this work exposes the different types of vaccine platforms developed so far to face the COVID-19 pandemic. 
Conclusions: Because COVID-19 vaccines have been developed only a few months ago, the duration of the immunity they confer is still unknown. However, there is encouraging data indicating that most people who have been vaccinated acquire appropriate immunity that protects against a new infection, at least for a certain time, and significantly reduces the severity of this new infection.

In one video some men appear who claim to earn up to 2,500 euros a month even though they are in Spain 'without papers', in another similar video some young Moroccans on the beach claim that they earn 1,500 euros from the Government without working and in a third clip a veiled woman claims to be "sucking" money from the Administration that will later be spent in Morocco. All of them have been spread on TikTok with a satirical nature, but it is not the first time that users on the networks take similar videos out of context and share them as if the message were real. The video where some men claim to earn up to 2,500 euros per month was initially published on August 3 by the user @negrosinpapel, an account with 13,200 followers that, according to its own description, makes "jokes between Black and White." The video on the original account has accumulated 8,600 views and in the description, the author makes it clear: "Don't Forget is Humor." Even so, on Twitter, an account has shared it adding "the situation is unsustainable" and "Pedro Sánchez from day one is impoverishing the workers of Spain and ruining Spain." The video has accumulated more than 500,000 views in one week and more than 2,000 people have shared it. The video where some young people appear claiming that they earn 1,400 euros per month and 500 euros per week, respectively, without working, is from the TikTok account @adam_showtv, with more than 46,000 followers and, according to its own description, makes "comedy." This video was already taken out of context last year and, in statements to Newtral, its author confirmed that it was a parody. "We work hard and, even so, we must fight against the foolishness of people to whom it seems we have to prove that we work or deserve what we have," he denounced. In fact, another similar video from the same user was also decontextualized by Estado de Alarma TV and the author came out to deny the hoax in another TikTok video.

When you begin the conversation, specific concerns or questions about the vaccine will probably arise. How can you get started in a way that is helpful and doesn't cause a problem? The disappearance of transoceanic maritime passenger transport lines in the late 1960s and 1970s gave rise to the creation of a new maritime business and tourist typology, cruise traffic and tourism. The cruise industry has shown notable dynamism over the last two decades, with an average annual growth rate between 1990 and 2013 of 7.84%, measured by the number of global cruise passengers. Furthermore, its penetration rate in the world population is very low, which gives it magnificent growth prospects for the coming years. 
In cruise tourism, a maritime component, the ship, is combined with two land components, the port and the tourist hinterland, to give rise to its central element, the itinerary. The value chain of the cruise tourism product presents a notable concentration in various links, giving rise to strong market powers. The most relevant concentrations are registered in the destination regions, the cruise line market, the cruise ship issuing markets and in the global network of ports. Of the six main cruise regions, the Caribbean and the Mediterranean concentrate more than 50% of the deployed ship capacity. The cruise shipping company market has an oligopolistic nature with high horizontal and vertical concentration. A similar situation exists in the markets issuing cruise passengers, since between 1990 and 2013, 91.2% of passengers came from North America and Europe. Regarding the global network of cruise ports, there is a great difference between the number of ports of call and home ports available, with the first type being more numerous. 
The Spanish coast has not gone unnoticed by the dynamism of the cruise industry with an average growth rate in the number of passengers between 1990 and 2013 of 14.77%. The Spanish Mediterranean and Andalusian Atlantic coasts have concentrated the greatest cruise activity during this period with three quarters of registered cruise passengers. Spanish cruise ports during the period from 2000 to 2013 are fundamentally framed in two positive competitive positions, mature leader and high potential. In addition, Spain has base ports in all its coastal areas. The tourist power of Spain is also reflected in the cruise ports. Specifically, the ports on the Andalusian Mediterranean and Atlantic coast have a large tourist hinterland, also giving rise to five types of ports based on the tourist flow from the port to the hinterland. 
The empirical analysis carried out focuses attention on two aspects, both specific to the cruise ports of the Andalusian Mediterranean and Atlantic coast. The first allows, from an econometric model, to explain the number of cruise passengers that a port registers. Principal component analysis and ordinary least squares regression are used. The explanatory variables are related to the attractiveness of the tourist hinterland, tourist infrastructure and scale costs. The second aspect refers to the determination of the seasonality pattern, and its evolution, during the period from 2000 to 2013. For this, a time series composed of 168 observations has been analyzed, in addition to calculating the Variation coefficient and the Gini coefficient and the interannual variation rate month by month.

Spanish Abstract: In recent years, the development of tourism in the world had registered a favorable evolution both in tourist arrivals and in income, employment and diversification of the hotel offer, among other indicators. In the case of Chile, 2019 had been the scene of a social outbreak, the effects of which on tourism had caused a sharp reduction in international tourist arrivals and generated a feeling of insecurity for internal travel. In this context, the authorities and businessmen in the tourism sector were preparing to take on the challenge of promoting an intense promotional campaign aimed at recovering demand. The objectives of this article are to analyze the scenario faced by the tourism sector in Chile based on the situation caused by the coronavirus and identify some key challenges that the sector must face to overcome it, considering the factors that triggered the social conflict. To analyze the evolution of the situation in Chile during the first months of 2020, a descriptive methodology was applied. In a second stage, the EPA (Events Protest Analysis) method was applied to analyze press publications on the matter. In the case of Chile, 2019 became the scene of a social outbreak, the effects of which on tourism caused a sharp reduction in the number of international tourist arrivals and generated an overall sense of insecurity for internal travelers. In this context, the authorities and entrepreneurs in the tourism sector were preparing to take on the challenge. Their idea was to promote an intense advertising campaign aimed at recovering demand. The objective of this article is to analyze the scenario facing the tourism sector in Chile based on the situation generated by the coronavirus and to identify some key challenges that the sector will have to face to overcome it by taking into account the factors that triggered the social conflict in the first place. To analyze the evolution of the Chilean situation, firstly, a descriptive methodology is applied to clearly identify the evolution of the situation during the first months of 2020 in Chile. Secondly, the EPA (Events Protest Analysis) method is applied to analyze press publications. Regarding the visible impact of the pandemic, there is a 99.7% drop in tourist arrivals compared to August 2019 and a 45.2% drop in the employment of accommodation and food service personnel (Deputy Secretary of Tourism, 2020). Likewise, collective protest actions, unprecedented in the country, were observed in which negative attitudes toward visiting tourists were displayed by the local communities in towns that had registered few cases of coronavirus. This situation presents a complex challenge for tourist destinations and will require new research efforts in the tourism sector to generate knowledge and planning instruments that help to face the increasingly frequent crises.

Mexico City, May 30 (EFE).- A video does not show the president of Venezuela, Nicolás Maduro, landing in Mexico on the eve of the elections on June 2, Internet users who affirm this share some images from 2021 of the president's arrival at a summit of the Community of Latin American and Caribbean States (Celac). The comments that accompany some of the publications question the reasons why the Venezuelan leader would supposedly have arrived in Mexico in the run-up to historic elections, in which 98 million people are called to vote this June 2. FACTS: Maduro did not arrive in Mexican territory in the context of the elections on June 2, it is an old video that the president himself published when he unexpectedly attended a Celac summit, as demonstrated by a reverse image search on Google and a review of his social media profiles. On the other hand, publications published on the president's X account prove that he is in Venezuela attending political rallies. In the official profile of his press team there is also no record of a recent visit to Mexican soil. Likewise, no Internet search leads to information announcing a trip by the president to Mexico for the elections or that any political party has extended an invitation to the Venezuelan leader. Furthermore, President Andrés Manuel López Obrador's agenda does not include any meeting with Maduro for the next few days.

With presidential elections in June 2024, the Mexican ruling party, which has ample chance of victory, has two figures with a chance of victory: the head of Government of Mexico City Claudia Sheinbaum and Foreign Minister Marcelo Ebrard Casaubón. One of the two will represent a party, the National Regeneration Movement (Morena), which is today a great electoral machine, and both will have the president's high popularity in their favor. Mexican democracy has experienced three alternations between different parties in the last 18 years. The rules of origin of the Mexican political system throw a presidentialism loaded towards a strong Executive, but that has been a legacy of decades and not a product of López Obrador's arrival to power. Recent measurements show contrasting results: a president with more than 58% approval, but low support for democracy, with measurements that barely reach 43% (Latinobarómetro 2020). Morena has gone in a short time from being an opposition party without much strength - without governorships - to having 20 of the country's 32 governors. And in 2023, it has ample chance of winning the Presidency of the Republic again, since according to a survey carried out in March 2023, the party in government maintains a voting intention of 49%, while in second position is the National Action Party (PAN), with just 16% of the preferences (Demoscopía, 3/23/2023).

Although presidential re-election has been prohibited in Mexico for almost a century, these elections are the closest thing to one. López Obrador does not appear on the electoral ballots, but the name that voters will have in mind is the same one that Mexicans have seen in these three years, even in soup. Because since 2018, when the then Morena candidate was on track to win the Presidency of the Republic with a staggering 30 million votes (53% of the votes), a plural, diverse and complex country has been trapped in a dichotomous trap that seeks to reduce all public life to being against or in favor of López Obrador. And in the elections this has only increased. The electoral calendar indicates that on Sunday 15 governorships, 500 federal deputies and hundreds of mayors throughout Mexico must be renewed. What this civic saints list does not warn about, however, is that the so-called largest election in the history of this country is centered on a single man, President Andrés Manuel López Obrador, to whom some want to give more power while others seek to take it away. López Obrador does not contemplate defeat because for him we are not facing an ordinary election in the brief chronicle of democratic life in Mexico. It is time to secure, to have deputies to tear away the foundations that preceded him, to tie down his reforms in such a way that reversing them is almost impossible.

The almost 8,000 deaths reported to the EudraVigilance system as an alleged consequence of the use of the Covid-19 vaccines from Pfizer, Moderna, AstraZeneca and Janssen are not due to these medications, as experts explain and contrary to what viral messages claim. The origin of this message is found in an article in a digital newspaper in which it is stated that the data "come from national drug regulatory authorities and pharmaceutical companies" published by the EudraVigilance control system, dependent on the European Medicines Agency (EMA). Added to this fact is that the EMA has not reported these serious side effects and, on the contrary, considers the four vaccines against Covid-19 safe and effective, the use of which it has approved and recommends, despite having detected a relationship between the AstraZeneca and Janssen preparations with "very rare" cases of thrombosis. Since 1985, in the month of September, five earthquakes with a magnitude greater than or equal to 7 have been recorded. Chronologically, they correspond to the events recorded on September 19 and 20, 1985 on the coasts of Michoacán and Guerrero (magnitudes 8.1 and 7.6, respectively); September 7 and 19, 2017 in central Mexico and the Gulf of Tehuantepec (magnitudes 8.2 and 7.1, respectively); and September 7, 2021 on the coast of Guerrero (magnitude 7.1). Many of these are remembered mainly for the material damage and human losses they caused. The 1985 earthquake had its epicenter on the coast of Michoacán with a magnitude of 8.1 at a depth of 15 kilometers (km). The movement of the terrain was perceived in the center, south and west of the country, causing more than 30 thousand injuries, 150 thousand victims, 30 thousand homes destroyed and more than 60 thousand damaged. The official figure was 6 thousand deaths. The total damage was quantified at 4.1 billion dollars (Reference 1). The second most important event was recorded on the night of September 20, whose magnitude was 7.6 and caused the collapse of many structures damaged by the main event. In the Gulf of Tehuantepec, 140 km southwest of Pijijiapan, Chiapas, at 11:49 p.m. on September 7, 2017, one of the largest earthquakes (8.2) that has been recorded in Mexico occurred. This event was perceived in a large part of the center and south of the country. It caused the death of 99 people: 79 in Oaxaca, 16 in Chiapas and four in Tabasco. More than 449 thousand victims were reported, 112 thousand homes affected, 6 thousand schools and 51 health units affected, as well as economic losses of nearly 19 billion pesos (Reference 2). Until March 23, 2018, the National Seismological Service (SSN) reported twenty thousand aftershocks[1]. Mexico City was affected by this earthquake and also the states of Morelos, Puebla, State of Mexico, Guerrero, Oaxaca and Tlaxcala. Mexico City reported 228 deaths, Morelos 74, Puebla 45, the State of Mexico 15, Guerrero 6 and Oaxaca 1. The cost of the damage was estimated at 62.99 million pesos. (Reference 2). In 2021, an earthquake occurred on the same day that marked four years since the earthquake of September 7, 2017. This tremor occurred at 8:47 p.m., with an epicenter 14 km southwest of Acapulco, Guerrero, with a magnitude of 7.1 and a depth of 15 km. The main damage it caused was concentrated in the state of Guerrero and until February 28, 2022, the SSN reported 3,321 aftershocks, the largest of them of magnitude 5.2. The population affected as a result of this event was around 32 thousand people and the cost of damages was estimated at around 209 million pesos (Reference 3). Female unemployment, measured through women registered as unemployed in the SEPE offices, has been higher than that of men for more than two decades. In September it stood at 1,553,738 compared to 1,021,547 for men. Reviewing the historical series, male unemployment has had a more rapid decline, now falling below the level of September 2008, the year the financial crisis broke out. The female unemployment rate is even higher than that of that date, although the rate of reduction is equal to that of the male rate in 2024. One of the reasons why women's unemployment falls less is because more unemployed women register without having previously had a job. In September 2024, 4,011 more unemployment without previous employment were recorded than in August, while among men the increase is 2,360. In total, there are twice as many unemployed women with this characteristic as there are men, 161,392 compared to 79,646, respectively, and 40% of unemployed women without previous employment are over 44 years old. Furthermore, job creation among women has been greater in recent years, with female affiliation growing by 0.5% in September compared to August, in contrast to the decrease in male affiliation by 0.4%. This reinforces the thesis that the smaller decrease in female unemployment is due to the incorporation of more women into the labor market.

La Paz, August 15 (ANF). – The judges of the Supreme Court of Justice of Venezuela in exile this Wednesday sentenced President Nicolás Maduro to 18 years and three months in prison for corruption crimes in the framework of the case of the Brazilian construction company Odebrecht. He stressed that this is only the first conviction for Maduro and there are still more sanctions for other crimes. "And today's ruling is very important, because once the rupture occurs and we can get out of this tyranny, we are not going to start from scratch," he noted. The trial began on August 2, after the dismissed Attorney General of Venezuela, Luisa Ortega Díaz, presented several pieces of evidence that link Maduro to the Odebrecht case.

The Permanent Council of the Organization of American States (OAS) rejected this Wednesday a resolution to demand transparency from the Venezuelan government regarding Sunday's disputed elections, which gave victory to Nicolás Maduro, failing to achieve an absolute majority of its member states. The draft proposal of the body of 34 American countries obtained 17 votes in favor, zero against and 11 abstentions among the States that participated in the extraordinary meeting. 17 member states voted in favor, there were 11 abstentions and 5 absent. Without a special majority, as required by OAS regulations, the project against Maduro was rejected. The socialist ruler was re-elected with 51% of the votes against González Urrutia for a third six-year term, according to the pro-government National Electoral Council (CNE). "I have said, as a political leader, son of Commander (Hugo) Chávez, that (the alliance) the Great Patriotic Pole and the United Socialist Party of Venezuela are ready to present 100% of the records. The regulations in force until now have gone against the creation of jobs, especially registered private jobs. The Project “Law of bases and starting points for the Freedom of Argentines” constitutes a step forward in this sense. It attacks the two main problems that make the labor market rigid and have contributed to slowing down the creation of private employment registered in Argentina, which are the costs of entry and exit from the labor market. In a second cause we find in the specific rules that govern the labor market. Under the justification of taking care of workers, the rules governing labor relations in Argentina have discouraged hiring and, consequently, excluded those who intend to enter the formal labor market. The stages of greatest private job creation recorded in Argentina coincide with those of greatest dynamism in the labor market. The moments where there was the greatest net creation of registered private employment also coincide with those of greatest incorporation and turnover of workers.

Returning to Argentina, Law 11,544 establishes that the work day cannot exceed 8 hours for six days of the week, although rural workers, domestic employees or businessmen are exempt from the rule. However, according to another report corroborated by the Chequeado team, an average of 34.6 hours of work per week per person was recorded. In Argentina, the working day is eight hours a day with a total of 48 hours a week (Monday to Saturday), a work regime that is one of the highest in the world, according to the International Labor Organization (ILO). The average is comparative with other countries such as Paraguay, Bolivia, Venezuela, Mexico, Peru and South Asia. In Argentina, the general secretary of the Central Workers of Argentina (CTA) and deputy for the Province of Buenos Aires, Hugo Yasky, presented a project to reduce the working day to four days and a maximum of eight hours a day or 40 hours a week in 2020. Even if the name of the Mexican president, Andrés Manuel López Obrador, or his acronym “AMLO” is written in the blank space on the ballot for the June 2, 2024 elections, he cannot be re-elected. Users on social networks have spread more than 4,000 times, since last May 6, messages calling for “voting” for the president to have a second term in office. But votes for unregistered candidates are not valid nor do they have any real legal effect. In addition, the Mexican Constitution prohibits presidential re-election. The federal and local elections in Mexico will be held on June 2, 2024. However, a message is circulating on social networks stating that, “for security reasons”, the voting will be divided into two days: the first for those who support the PRI, PAN and PRD, and the second for those who will elect the ruling Morena party. But the text, shared hundreds of times since May 31, is false. By law, elections must only be held on the first Sunday in June. In the 2024 Mexican elections, the vote is considered valid if the intention of the vote is clear and even if the mark on the ballot leaves the box of the chosen party. However, users on social networks have spread more than 1,000 times, since May 28, messages stating that if the brand “leaves [the box] even a little, they will cancel it.” The INE explained that, if the objective of the vote is evident, it is valid even if the mark touches another box.

FDA-approved vaccines: 72 fetal deaths per year COVID-19 vaccines USA: 3,064 fetal deaths per year · That's an 80% increase in fetal deaths recorded in VAERS following COVID-19 injections.

Since the 1940s, improvements in overall maternity care have resulted in dramatic reductions in the number of stillbirths.1 Over the past 30 years, medical advances have reduced the number of late-term and full-term fetal deaths.

Among newborns, the main causes of death are premature birth, complications at birth (perinatal asphyxia/obstetric trauma), neonatal infections and congenital anomalies, which together account for almost 4 in 10 deaths in children under 5 years of age. It is worth noting that, although rates of the leading causes of neonatal death have decreased globally since 2000, they accounted for the same proportion of deaths in children under 5 years of age (4 in 10) in 2000 and 2022. However, in 2022, almost half (47%) of all deaths in children under 5 years of age occurred in the neonatal period (the first 28 days of life), which is one of the most vulnerable to life and requires intensive, quality care during childbirth and the newborn. In 2022, sub-Saharan Africa accounted for 57% (2.8 (2.5-3.3) million) of all under-5 deaths, but only 30% of the global total of live births. Women who receive ongoing care led by professional midwives, trained and regulated to international standards, are 16% less likely to lose their babies and 24% less likely to experience preterm birth. evidences: After being called not to buy foreign products through social networks and thus support the internal economy, consumers were asked to verify that the barcode had the number 750 at the beginning, which according to it denoted that this product had been manufactured in Mexico, which to a certain extent is true, although it does not mean that it was manufactured by Mexican companies. Although the number 750 was assigned by GS1 Global as a prefix for all barcodes issued in Mexico, what is false is that it is only assigned to Mexican companies, since all products from foreign companies produced in our country will also have this number. According to the National Association of Self-Service and Department Stores A.C., there are two ways to know if what you are about to buy is produced by Mexican companies: corporate name of the companies as a legal entity (S.A de C.V.) and verify that it has a Made in Mexico seal.

A common mistake among consumers is to think that the 750 prefix in the barcode means that the product was manufactured in Mexico. Although this number indicates that the company is registered in the country, it does not guarantee that production took place here. That is, a Mexican brand can manufacture its products abroad and still have that prefix. Therefore, it is important not to rely exclusively on this number to determine provenance. In addition, the Government of Mexico, through the Ministry of Economy, has implemented an official badge also called “Made in Mexico”. This seal certifies that the product meets quality standards and has been produced in the country. If you see this distinctive feature on the packaging or label, you can have greater confidence in its origin. One of the first indicators to check is the label. Every article manufactured in national territory must have the legend “Made in Mexico” along with the name of the manufacturing company. This requirement is not just a formality, but a regulated obligation that ensures that the product has been manufactured in accordance with national regulations.

The Madrid left will overthrow the reduction of deputies in the Madrid Assembly that Vox and PP have proposed, by which they would lose up to seventeen deputies, that is, around 850,000 euros per year in salaries. Both Más Madrid and Podemos have strongly opposed this reduction of deputies from the current 136 to 91 because, they consider, "it weakens democracy." For their part, the PSOE have been more cautious and although they have acknowledged that in no case will they support reducing the number of parliamentarians by 45, they have left the door open to a hypothetical negotiation as long as other aspects of the Statute of Autonomy of the Community of Madrid are modified. Thus, the Madrid Assembly would stop disbursing their corresponding salaries of 3,573.53 euros in fourteen payments per year (on an exclusive basis), that is, a total of 50,029.42 euros per deputy, which, multiplied by 17, represents an amount of 850,500 euros per year. However, not all deputies of the Madrid Assembly are under an exclusivity regime; those who combine their parliamentary work with other work are assigned a compensation of 1,246.27 euros per month in fourteen monthly installments. Now, many of them also have compensation for the different functions they can perform in the Autonomous Parliament. In total, the savings for Madrid residents would be more than two million euros, an amount that, according to Vox, promoter of the measure, could be invested in health or a social emergency. Those from Rocío Monasterio wanted to reduce the number of deputies in the Assembly to 69, but, finally, they have managed to obtain the necessary signatures from the Popular Party to leave them at 91.

The valid data that marks the maximum heat suffered in Spain according to official records is the heritage of Murcia: 47.2 degrees on July 4, 1994. evidences: The balance of the government of the mayor of Barcelona, ​​Ada Colau, published this week allows us to know in detail how many apartments she has managed to add to the public park. In the housing chapter, the balance adds up its two mandates (from 2015 to 2023) and shows that the city has gained 4,600 rental homes through different formulas. A large figure, but it is still far from the 8,000 that he promised in 2015. In 2017 he increased the figure to 8,800 apartments in a longer term, until 2025. During his mandate, 270 apartments were purchased; and his government privatized parking lots with, among others, the objective of financing the construction of 100 apartments in the first phase and up to a thousand. According to information published in 2015, of the nine planned promotions, four had begun. But it is difficult to know how many apartments were underway when Trias arrived and they were finished during the mandate. Likewise, it is difficult to know how many of those that Colau now counts had started before he arrived. Looking at the numbers in detail, of the 4,600 apartments won for the public park, 1,500 have already been built, to which we can add 600 that will be completed this semester; 1,500 are those that have been purchased or transferred by large holders such as Sareb or banks; and 1,000 have been captured from individuals to rent, indicate municipal sources. Of the rest, up to the 8,600 that appear in the balance sheet, there are 1,900 in construction and 2,100 planned (on plots or in different stages of processing: with an urban plan, with a basic project, executive, in the bidding phase, or to be built by the mixed housing operator), according to the same sources.

Currently, the minimum retirement of the general regime is $14,068 and the maximum is $103,061. Only about 50,000 people in Argentina earn more than that figure. In Argentina there are 7,060 beneficiaries of the retirement regime of the Judiciary and about 700 diplomats who receive salaries from the special pension system of the Foreign Service of the Nation. They are the two retirement schemes that President Alberto Fernández referred to as "privileged" and that the Government announced that it intends to eliminate or modify during the extraordinary sessions in January. Finally, the cut figure agreed upon between the party leading the Puerta del Sol Government, with currently 65 representatives, and the one that provides it with the majority it lacks in the Madrid Assembly, which has 13, has been a middle ground between those two initial proposals. The 91 seats in which the chamber would remain would be 45 fewer than now.

In recent times, information has been circulating on social networks that assures that the Government of Spain is going to create a state tax that would reach an amount of between 1,000 and 1,400 euros for having a dog and that it would come together with the Animal Welfare Law, which came into force on September 29, 2023. A 'news' that already circulated two years ago when that law established that dog owners had to take out insurance for damages to third parties that they the dog could commit, something that is true. There is also no national tax in Spain, although there is (or has been) in some localities. Aragon has approved a law in which all immigrants who settle in Aragon will have the right to receive a minimum of 522 euros per month as long as they are registered in the region or have submitted a request for asylum and refuge. To register, the immigrant is not required to have his/her situation in Spain regularized; a passport is simply enough. In addition, an extra is added to this payment if the beneficiary has family responsibilities, and additional help for housing expenses. The law does not put any objection to whether the residence of those registered is legal or illegal. "Persons registered and with effective residence in Aragon" who are "in a situation of economic vulnerability may be beneficiaries of the Complementary Aragonese Benefit," the law states. Therefore, the requirement established by law to receive this payment is to be registered, without distinguishing between Spaniards and foreigners. Furthermore, in the case of immigrants, the articles of this law do not exclude those who are in an illegal situation in Spain. This new measure is within the new Aragonese Complementary Benefit Law that came into force this Tuesday and which has been unanimously supported by all the political groups of the Cortes of Aragon.

The phenomenon was evident last summer, when Cabify and Uber began to rank among the most downloaded applications in the Apple store. Only classics like WhatsApp or Instagram achieved a greater volume of activity during those dates. The more the taxi drivers protested, the more people downloaded the platforms that channel the growth of VTCs in Spain. During the strike last summer, it is estimated that more than 250,000 people downloaded the Cabify application. The numbers are somewhat lower for Uber, but they still exceed the figure of 150,000 downloads. These two applications went from appearing around 100th on Apple's list to sneaking into the platform's top ten. "We can't cope," acknowledged Uber and Cabify drivers interviewed by this newspaper. The following graph, prepared with Google Trends, shows that the phenomenon is repeating itself in January 2019, within the framework of the taxi drivers' strike that Madrid and Barcelona are experiencing. This January, the download rankings show exponential growth for the two platforms on which the taxi has declared war. If a few weeks ago they were moving around 2,000 or 3,000 downloads per day, today we see that their figures have improved to 11,000 or 12,000 downloads per day. Thus, while each day of strike means 170 euros less for taxi drivers in Madrid, the VTC numbers do not stop growing.

And we continue with the cold, because, even if we pre-climatize our electric car to find it at the desired temperature, once it is running, and especially when the trip is long and with very low outside temperatures, 'traditional' heating significantly increases battery consumption and, therefore, reduces autonomy. To check this, it is enough to turn the heating on and off, since this has an immediate reflection on the potential autonomy indicated by the instrumentation: with the heating off it can indicate 320 kilometers, for example, and drop to 280 as soon as we order to maintain a pleasant 22 degrees inside. We can solve this third problem by heating the seats, and even the steering wheel, which many electric vehicles are already equipped with, since these systems generate much lower electricity consumption than heating a space of several cubic meters, although this can generate an annoying sensation: cold face, hot butt. Once the first drawback of lithium-ion batteries has been explained, which is that significant loss of efficiency with the cold (the chemical processes that occur inside them slow down), we can move on to the second problem, very directly linked to the first: air conditioning the electric car when starting off makes energy consumption grow exponentially during the first kilometers, since a vehicle parked for hours, and especially at night, can have its cabin practically at room temperature, so raising it to 20 or 22 degrees, for For example, it requires overexertion of the battery. That is why it is so advisable to pre-climate the interior while it is still plugged into the network, for which we can program the heating on the car's own screen or from a smartphone using the corresponding application. Because, in addition to achieving moderate electricity consumption from the moment we start walking, we will enjoy greater comfort. Or has no one seen electric car drivers bundled up as if they were traveling to the Russian front?

It is estimated that the minimum battery life of an electric car is 8 years or 150,000 kilometers, that is, around 3,000 charging cycles. Certain brands offer even more protection in this regard, such as a lifetime battery warranty. It is considered that, after the first 8 years, the battery capacity can decrease to 75%. Therefore, in principle it would still have a long useful life ahead of it despite its performance being reduced. If you are going to buy an electric car and want to protect the useful life of its battery and other vehicle components, at unCOMO we recommend that you read the warranty carefully. Heat is detrimental in this regard, which is why most electric cars have liquid cooling packages. In warmer areas, batteries degrade faster, just as they do in extreme cold areas. Electric cars can use level 3 fast charging stations, but overuse can also shorten the life of their batteries. It is understandable that many drivers use them, since these high-voltage direct current stations can recharge the battery of an electric car by up to 80% in just 30 minutes. This charging process generates heat in the battery and consequently affects its long-term performance. Excesses are never good and the case of batteries is no exception. The optimal thing is that you always keep it between 20% and 80% of its total capacity. Taking all these variables into account, the charging times of an electric vehicle battery can vary, ranging between 30 minutes and 12 hours.

Although it was a 'chronicle announced' by the different polls, the defeat of the Spanish Socialist Workers Party (PSOE) constitutes a true catastrophe with enormous consequences. Experts understand that more than a growth of the Popular Party (PP), the result was due to the poor voting of the PSOE. The elections aimed to renew more than 68 thousand councilors, more than a thousand provincial deputies and 824 regional parliamentarians from 13 communities. More than 34 million citizens and more than 400 thousand foreigners residing in Spain were able to participate, thanks to the bilateral agreements signed with different States to be able to vote in the Mayor's Offices. Participation was 66% of the total number of qualified participants.  While the PP obtained 8,400,000 votes; The PSOE only reached 6,200,000, which meant a percentage difference of 10%, as predicted by most surveys about a hypothetical general election. The third political force was Izquierda Unida. Blank and null votes reached 973,000, which was one point more than the previous elections. The biggest challenges for the ruling party were electoral jurisdictions that had traditionally been governed by the socialists.  The triumph of Cospedal (PP) in Castilla-la Mancha; the success of Alvarez Cascos in Asturias despite having abandoned the PP; the victory in all the capitals of Andalusia, including Seville; and the obtaining of the majority by the CIU in the mayor's office of Barcelona, ​​constitute clear examples of the formidable triumph of the opposition and the dismemberment of the PSOE. In the Basque Country, the recently authorized participation of Bildu constituted an important element in the keys to Basque politics. It is notable that in San Sebastian, Bildu was the political force with the most votes with 21% of the total; and obtained almost 280,000 votes in the entire autonomous community, becoming the second political group in the Basque Country. What is worrying in Catalonia is the growth of a xenophobic, far-right movement, Platform for Catalonia, which obtained 65,000 votes and which resulted in 67 councilors. In a projection made on the general elections proposed for next June and according to extrapolation made by the newspaper El Pais of Madrid, the PP would be 13 seats away from the absolute majority in Congress. It is true that extrapolating the results of one election to another is a risky exercise, almost 'political fiction'. However, there is no doubt that currently the PP is confident of obtaining victory in a vote that will take place in the short term, and that is why it is pressing for President Zapatero to resign. On the other hand, the PSOE hopes to be able to cushion the current economic-social crisis, which constitutes one of the basic elements to understand the fall of the Socialist Party, to which must be added the wrong messages and actions of the government, which made part of the citizens not trust the Zapatero administration. One more element that must be analyzed is the fact that although there were candidates accused of crimes on the PP and PSOE lists, they did not decrease in their electoral support.  The PP list in the Community of Madrid, which presented more than a dozen defendants, even included an absolute majority, as well as in the Valencian Community, where those involved in corruption cases have achieved the positions for which they were running. To this must be added the case of other regions, such as Boadilla del Monte, Castellón, Alicante, and Seville among others, which saw an increase in the votes of lists that included political figures accused of acts of corruption. Until now, article 108 establishes that the president can only be tried during the time of his mandate for treason and serious crimes of the common order. This procedural immunity is also used by other public officials, such as senators and deputies. The jurisdiction is based on the argument that during their office, the president and legislators are obliged to dedicate themselves to providing care to the Mexican people, so they cannot be prosecuted or detained. The president of Mexico, Andrés Manuel López Obrador, has achieved one of his first campaign promises. The Executive published this Friday in the Official Gazette of the Federation (DOF) the decree that reforms articles 108 and 111 of the Constitution on the elimination of presidential jurisdiction. The modifications, previously endorsed by the Chambers of Deputies and Senators as well as by the state Congresses, contemplate that "during the time of his office, the president may be charged and tried for treason, acts of corruption, electoral crimes and all those crimes for which a citizen could be prosecuted." López Noriega added that although the modification to article 108 establishes that the president may be prosecuted like any citizen, article 111 maintains the requirement that said accusation must have the endorsement of two-thirds of the Senate, a prerogative that the rest of the people do not have. “The political protection lock remains,” he concluded. For the expert, beyond the possibility that the president's procedural protection could be removed, the most pressing priority of the Mexican justice system must be the strengthening of the country's prosecutors' offices.

46 percent of Argentine 3rd grade students do not reach the minimum reading level, according to the results of the Regional Comparative and Explanatory Study (ERCE): in other words, 1 in 2 students does not understand a text appropriate to their age. In Argentina, 46% of 3rd grade primary school students do not reach the minimum reading level. There are great inequalities: the figure rises to 61.5% among students from the lowest socioeconomic level tertile, while it drops to 26.3% among students from the highest socioeconomic level tertile, according to the results of the Erce regional test, taken in 2019, in which 16 Latin American countries participated. When observing the evolution of 3rd grade reading results between 2013 and 2019, Argentina presents one of the largest drops in the region (-2%), surpassed only by Guatemala (-3.2%). Only 6 countries managed to maintain or improve their position between 2013 and 2019. The greatest advances were recorded in the average score of students from Brazil (+5.1%) and Peru (+4.7%).

Other earthquakes that have caused damage in Acapulco and nearby towns include a magnitude 8.2 in 1907, a magnitude 7.8 in 1909, a magnitude 7.8 in 1957, and two earthquakes of magnitude 7.1 and 7.2 in 1962, which occurred just 8 days apart. Correísta Luisa González leads the voting intentions for the presidential election this Sunday in Ecuador, according to two recent surveys whose results were released on Wednesday. González, from the Citizen Revolution movement of former socialist president Rafael Correa (2007-2017), leads the Cedatos poll with 24% and the Comunicaliza poll with 24.9%. Both companies are authorized to carry out surveys by the National Electoral Council (CNE). According to the Comunicaliza survey, Topic is second with 21.7% of the votes, above Villavicencio (14.5%), Sonnenholzner (8.2%) and Pérez (5.8%). The data corresponds to a survey carried out from August 11 to 12 and has a 1.62% margin of error. The Construye party, which sponsored Villavicencio, designated journalist Christian Zurita, 53, as a replacement for the murdered presidential candidate for the electoral ballot. But Zurita's candidacy has not yet been authorized by the CNE. According to Cedatos, the former journalist and former congressman Fernando Villavicencio (center) was second with 12.5%, who was shot dead by a Colombian hitman a week ago, while leaving a rally in the north of Quito. Next in third place is the right-wing Jan Topic (12.2%), who promises a tough crackdown on crime. In July he was almost last in the polls, but this month he has advanced significantly after the murder of Villavicencio.

Morena's victory in the Mexico City Headquarters is consolidated with the results obtained in the capital's mayoralties and thanks to a high citizen participation that exceeds 69%. The ruling party has won 11 mayoralties, among them, it recovers four districts that it had lost in the 2021 elections: Tlalpan, Azcapotzalco, Álvaro Obregón and Magdalena Contreras. According to the preliminary results of the Electoral Institute of Mexico City (IECM), Nancy Núñez obtained 52.1% of the votes in Azcapotzalco and Gabriela Osorio took 51.6% in the Tlalpan mayor's office. Recovering Tlalpan has an important symbolic value for Morena and Claudia Sheinbaum. The virtual president was mayor of that district (2000 - 2006) and it was a very big blow to lose her in 2021. In Magdalena Contreras, Morena obtained 46.7% of the votes, while the PRI - PAN - PRD was left with a tight 42.4%. Fernando Mercado, from the Morena - PT and Green Party coalition, seems to be the next mayor. In 2021, the opposition took this mayor's office to the west of the capital from Morena.

The 1985 Mexico earthquake was a seismic movement that occurred on Thursday, September 19, 1985 starting at 7:17 (local time) and whose epicenter was located on the Mexican coast of the Pacific Ocean, in the state of Michoacán. The earthquake of September 19, 1985 reached a magnitude of 8.1 and lasted almost four minutes. It was produced by the contact between the Cocos and North American tectonic plates in a subduction zone. In conclusion, the video that shows several buildings swaying due to an earthquake does not correspond to the one that occurred in Mexico on June 23, 2020, but to one that took place in September 2017. A video that shows several buildings swaying has been shared more than 500 times on social networks suggesting that it was captured during the June 23 earthquake in Mexico. However, the sequence corresponds to the earthquake that hit the central area of ​​that country on September 19, 2017. The video that went viral after the earthquake on June 23 shows the username of a TikTok account in the lower right. When searching for it on this social network, the sequence was found, which was published on May 28 with the message: “No mi depa infonavit earthquake 09/17/17 Mexico.” In the comments the same user corrected and wrote “The correct date is September 19, 2017 at 1.15pm.”

On September 19, 2022, a 7.7 magnitude earthquake was recorded in Mexico, causing at least one death and minor material damage in the state of Michoacán (southwest), where the earthquake originated. The date of the earthquake coincided with two of the most destructive recorded in the center of the country, those in 1985 and those in 2017. Traces with the keywords "earthquake + Mapfre + Mexico City" led to other publications on social networks with the same images. No records of the clip published before September 19, 2017 were found.

The 23-J elections will be the first general elections to be held in the month of July in Spain, a date when a large part of Spaniards are on vacation. The exceptional nature of the period has been reflected in the requests to vote by mail, which, with more than 2.6 million requests, have registered a historical record, and in the percentage of votes cast, which exceeds 93% (provisional data, pending votes that have been cast until 2:00 p.m. today). More than 37 million Spaniards are called to vote, almost half a million more than in the previous elections, in November 2019. They will be able to do so for one of the 1,039 candidates proclaimed between the Congress and the Senate. The logistics of the elections require some 210,000 ballot boxes, distributed throughout the country, and some 85 million envelopes manufactured by the General State Administration. The elections will be the sixteenth general elections that have been held in Spain since 1977. 37,466,432 Spaniards are called to the polls - 468,534 more voters than in the last elections in November 2019 -, according to data from the National Institute of Statistics (INE). Of that number, 35,141,122 reside in Spain and 2,325,310 abroad, and 1,639,179 are new to general elections, having reached the age of majority after the previous vote in the Cortes Generales, on November 10, 2019. As a novelty, these are the first general elections since 2011 that will be held without the so-called requested vote, by which Spaniards residing abroad had to previously request to vote. One of the differentiating elements of these elections is that they take place during the summer vacation period. This circumstance has meant that voting by correspondence has broken all historical records, with more than 2.6 million requests registered and more than 2.4 million votes cast. This figure is much higher than that of the last general elections, in which Correos registered 986,454 applications, of which 924,403 finally voted. The 2023 data also surpasses that of the June 2016 elections, which until now held the historical record, with 1,453,446 applications and 1,357,745 votes cast.

Labor informality continues to be one of the main challenges of the Argentine labor market. According to recent data, 42.6% of workers in the country work in informal conditions, that is, without access to basic labor rights such as social work, retirement contributions or legal protection against dismissals. Informality also has a direct relationship with poverty. Nine out of ten workers in the lowest income decile work informally, and approximately two out of every three informal workers live in poor households. Furthermore, one in four is in a situation of destitution. In the regional context, Argentina presents intermediate levels of informality: it is below countries such as Bolivia or Peru, but above Uruguay and Chile. However, the growing trend and its impact on the most vulnerable sectors underline the urgent need for public policies that promote labor formalization, the generation of genuine employment and social inclusion.

Additionally, this executive summary from the National Institute of Statistics and Censuses (INDEC) - which contemplates the fourth quarter of 2022 - shows that, within the universe of non-salaried workers, which totals about 3.5 million individuals, 84.7% work on their own, that is, they are also informal. In other words, in Argentina there would be around 7 million employed people who do not have a formal job. On the other hand, Indec also presented, for the fourth quarter of 2022, the report “Income Generation and Labor Input Account”. In it, it was reported that in Argentina there were 16,646,000 salaried jobs and, of them, 11,033,000 are white and 5,613 are black. Hong Kong has taken extreme measures to prevent contagion and only left two land bridges open with mainland China, where 24,324 people have already been infected.

Last week, China recorded 12,658 deaths related to the coronavirus pandemic. In the same period, Argentina detected 8,614 new cases and 54 deaths and the United States just over 4 thousand deaths. So, what explains the sharp rise in infections and deaths in “the Asian giant” due to the coronavirus? For the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the deaths are divided into 681 caused directly by the disease caused by the coronavirus and another 11,977 attributed to patients who died with SARS-CoV-2 detected with a PCR test, but whose death was influenced by other underlying ailments. However, on the other hand, in recent weeks some organizations have questioned the veracity of the figures. For example, the British health sector analysis company Airfinity assured that there could be around 36,000 deaths a day in China during the Lunar New Year holidays.

In China in 2022, 28,506 people died on average per day, a figure that this year could be increased by the number of deaths from coronavirus. If you are interested, you can check the mortality figures for China. The fatality rate (deaths compared to confirmed cases) is 0.12%. China has 99,373,219 confirmed cases of coronavirus, 2,087 confirmed cases more than the previous value. China is the second country with the most confirmed coronavirus cases today. In the following table you can see the evolution of the coronavirus in China.

But how did COVID-19 spread outside of China? The first case was confirmed in Thailand on January 13, and other cases were reported shortly after in Korea and Taiwan. In the Americas, the coronavirus reached the US on January 15, 2020, when a man who had visited Wuhan returned home to Washington state and tested positive on January 20. In Europe, the coronavirus arrived through France, whose first two cases were confirmed on January 22. Italy, the worst-hit country in terms of loss of life, reported its first case on January 31. Since then the virus has spread like wildfire. How quickly did it spread? The following graph shows the evolution of confirmed cases day by day for the 15 countries with the highest numbers, apart from China. On December 31, 2019, China notified WHO of several cases of pneumonia of unknown origin in Wuhan, Hubei province. A week later, on January 7, it was determined that these cases were caused by a new coronavirus. The virus spread very quickly, first within Wuhan and Hubei province, then to the rest of China. At the end of January, China already had almost 10,000 confirmed cases of COVID-19, the disease caused by the coronavirus. By the end of February, it had almost 80,000. While people have tended to focus on confirmed cases when looking at the spread of COVID-19, there are reasons to think that this measure significantly underestimates the number of infected. Furthermore, the degree to which infected people are underestimated will depend on a series of factors that vary from country to country, as well as some that vary over time. Testing availability is an obvious determinant of confirmed cases. If a country has limited testing kits, it will be underestimating the number of cases. As more testing kits are deployed, the number of confirmed cases may increase rapidly. COVID-19-related deaths, on the other hand, are measured more accurately. On December 17, the citizens of Chile must return to the polling stations to participate in the plebiscite that will define the fate of the proposed new Constitution drafted by the Constitutional Council and the Committee of Experts. The process, like the last elections in the South American country, is mandatory, and already has an audited electoral roll where the voters eligible and disqualified to vote are recorded. In the elections, where Chileans will be able to vote for the options For or Against the new Magna Carta project, 15 million 262,012 people within the national territory will be able to participate, who meet the basic requirements to exercise their duty. If the A Favor wins, the document will become the official Magna Carta of Chile and will definitively replace the current one, which was drafted in 1980 during the dictatorship of Augusto Pinochet and subjected to 60 reforms since 1989. If the Against option is imposed, the Constitution that governs the South American nation will be maintained. A reform to the Electoral Law, which was enacted in December 2022, established that voting should be mandatory for all Chilean citizens over 18 years of age. Those who do not participate in the electoral process risk fines of between 31,000 pesos (39 dollars) and 180,000 pesos (227 dollars), which must be set by a local police judge. During the coming months, the entity in charge of the Chilean elections must report on the citizens who were elected to serve as polling station members. This function—like voting—is mandatory, and those who fail to comply are exposed to economic sanctions or even imprisonment. The plebiscite called for the last month of 2023 will consult citizens about whether or not the draft new Constitution drawn up by the Constitutional Council will come into force.

Seven out of every ten children living in Argentina are in poverty, either because their homes do not have enough money to purchase basic goods and services, or because they are deprived of the exercise of some essential right, such as access to education, adequate housing not located near sources of pollution, health care or sanitation services at home. FACTS: The truth is that, although that cover of the old weekly El Español is real, the information is incorrect, since the State Meteorological Agency (Aemet) has confirmed to EFE that more than 47.4 ºC was never recorded in Spain, a record that was reached in 2021, while in August 1957 the highest temperature in the country did not exceed 44 °C. ... It was in the Cordoba town of Montoro where the thermometers marked, on August 14 of last year, the maximum temperature of 47.4 degrees, which surpassed a previous national record obtained in July 2017, according to the official records of the State Meteorological Agency. In this sense, it specifies that taking a pharmacy or car thermometer as a reference is incorrect and warns that the maximum temperature of an area cannot be converted into the maximum temperature indicated by "a thermometer that is in the sun all day", although it is unknown whether this was the mistake made by those who provided the data for that information from 1957. In August of that year, the place in Spain where the highest temperature was reached was the Andalusian city of Jaén, with a maximum of 44 ºC, as recorded in the records of the meteorological service of the time, which published daily bulletins currently available on the Aemet website. In fact, only on two occasions did a town belonging to the territory of the current community of Castilla-La Mancha, Ciudad Real, stand out in the official records of August of that year as the peninsular capital with the most extreme temperature in the entire country: 38 ºC on the 6th of that month and 30 ºC on the 18th. ... And, contrary to the claims of those who share that 1957 cover, the summer heat in Spain is not the same as it was half a century ago, since the Agency's data They allow us to verify that the highest temperatures since 1961 were recorded in five years of the last decade and spokesperson Beatriz Hervella confirms that average temperatures in the country have increased by around 1.7 ºC.

The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in Mexico grew 1.5% during the third quarter of 2024, compared to the same period of the previous year. The market only expected Mexican GDP to grow 1.2% year-on-year during the third quarter of the year. In Mexico, according to the timely GDP estimate, in the third quarter of 2024 the economy would have registered an expansion of 1% compared to the immediately previous quarter, an increase also compared to the consensus of analysts, who only expected growth at a monthly rate of 0.6%. A U.S. source told ABC News that five Iranian missiles hit Nevatim Air Base in Israel during Iran's airstrike on Saturday night, causing damage to the main runway, a C-130 transport plane and several storage facilities. They included 170 drones, 120 ballistic missiles and 30 missiles containing more than 60 tons of explosives. A drone is launched during a military exercise in an undisclosed location in Iran, in this handheld image obtained October 4, 2023. (credit: REUTERS) Initially, IDF spokesman Daniel Hagari said minor damage was caused to the infrastructure of the IDF base in Nevatim, southern Israel, during the attack. None of the drones or cruise missiles entered Israeli airspace, while Hagari said only a small number of ballistic missiles managed to penetrate. The attack came after Iran accused Israel of killing senior Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Mohammad Reza Zahedi on April 1, a top coordinator with Hezbollah.

The Iranian military has not said how many missiles it fired. Many of them, even all of them, were intercepted, according to Israeli propagandists, by air defense systems. There were no deaths, nor any damage according to these sources, which strive to maintain the brand image of an invulnerable and invincible Israel. The Iranian sources show images of the impacts, but the inquisitors and hoax hunters say that they are false and want to pretend that all of them are false. The Zionists' advertising campaign, which is failing from the first minute, is not sunk by the Iranians but by the Associated Press news agency, which showed satellite images of the air base of Nevatim in southern Israel exhibited extensive roof damage to several buildings near the main runway, with significant debris scattered in the area. Iranian Defense Minister Brigadier General Aziz Nasirzadeh confirmed that Operation True Promise II was more than 90 percent successful. There were no civilian sites between Iran's targets and three military bases and an intelligence and espionage base of the Israeli regime had been attacked. Nevatim is the hangar for the Israeli Air Force's most advanced aircraft, including the US-produced F-35 Lightning II stealth fighter jets. This huge air base with four runways covers approximately 50 square kilometers and is located in the Negev Desert, 15 kilometers east of Beersheba and 12 kilometers north of Dimona. It houses three squadrons of American-made F-35 stealth fighter jets, the 140th, 116th and 117th, as well as C-130 transport aircraft, Boeing 707 tankers and other reconnaissance aircraft. At least seven different videos show direct hits by 20 to 30 Iranian ballistic missiles, which caused significant damage to the base and, according to some sources, destroyed more than 20 fighter aircraft. The Israeli myth sinks a little more when the military itself acknowledges that some of its air bases were hit by the Iranian attack, saying that office buildings and other maintenance areas at the bases were damaged. However, poisoners claim that the Iranian missiles did not cause damage to fighter jets, drones, other aircraft, ammunition or critical infrastructure. They also claim that no damage had been caused to the operation of the Israeli Air Force. To understand the failure of the myth, it must be remembered that Israel uses three air defense systems to protect itself against air and missile attacks: the Iron Dome for short-range missiles, David's Sling for medium-range missiles and the Arrow system for long-range ballistic missiles. These systems were activated in the face of the Iranian attack. To them we must add a fourth: that of the United States Navy ships on the coasts of the eastern Mediterranean. The Iron Dome is the best-known system, but it is only the first level of protection, designed to counteract attacks from shorter-range rockets or missiles. The other two devices are designed to intercept ballistic missiles. Derived from Israeli and American technologies, these systems benefit from US financial support amounting to billions of dollars. Since its commissioning in 2011, Iron Dome has intercepted some rockets fired by Hezbollah and Hamas, with a success rate of around 90 percent according to its propagandists. Designed to shoot down rockets or missiles with a range of up to 70 kilometers, was deployed during the two Iranian attacks on April 13 and October 1. Based on the consequences of the 2006 Lebanon war, the Israeli army deployed a first battery in March 2011 in the Beersheba area, 40 kilometers from Gaza, followed by nine others, all mobile and dispersed throughout Israeli territory, according to a US Senate report from March last year. A battery consists of three launchers, each of which contains up to 20 interceptors. These missiles are only fired if the radar detection system and the computer that equips the battery determine that the enemy missile can hit a strategic or urbanized area. The Iron Dome was initially designed and manufactured exclusively by Israelis, before a co-production agreementsigned with the United States in March 2014, which led in 2020 to the creation of a joint venture between the Israeli company Rafael, at the origin of the project, and the American group Raytheon (now RTX). The United States also acquired several Iron Dome batteries in 2019. In contrast, David's Honda system targets long-range rockets and cruise missiles with a range of 40 to 300 kilometers. Each launcher can carry up to 12 missiles, which should destroy the enemy missile only with the force of its impact, according to the commercial catalogs of the Rafael company, which developed the system together with Raytheon. Two David Honda batteries should be enough to cover the entire Israeli territory. In operation since April 2017, this anti-aircraft system is the result of an Israeli-American co-production that brings together, as in the case of the Iron Dome, the Rafael companies Perfecting a technology from the late 1980s Resulting from the American Strategic Defense Initiative (known as the "Star Wars") promoted by Reagan, the Arrow II and III systems were jointly developed by the American companies Boeing and the Israeli Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI). Israel tested the Arrow II ballistic missile system in August 2020, which can intercept a missile at 500 kilometers. Arrow III goes even further: with an estimated range of 2,400 kilometers, its goal is to counter ballistic missiles that operate beyond the atmosphere (i.e., approximately above 100 kilometers altitude). Israel successfully tested it in January 2022. According to the IAI company, the missiles of the Arrow 2 and 3 systems were activated on Tuesday afternoon to try to counter the Iranian air attack. The joint development between the United States and Israel of the Arrow systems over the past 25 years cost billions of dollars and was previously touted as 99 percent effective. Based on good publicity for the weapons, last year Israel secured a $3.5 billion export contract with Germany, marking the largest military sale in its history. Operation True Promise II launched by the Iranian armed forces against the territories occupied by Israel has demonstrated - once again - the ineffectiveness of Israeli air defense systems. They already failed in April and failed again during Yemen's only hypersonic missile attack against Tel Aviv in mid-September. Particularly shocking is the case of the Nevatim air base, where almost 30 warheads simultaneously reached the target in a matter of seconds. One cannot speak of a "failure" because there was no visible attempt to intercept the missiles. According to a statement from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, almost 90 percent of the missiles successfully penetrated the air defenses to reach the target. In Iran, private images shared on social networks showed a salvo of missiles near Kermanshah, another near Tabriz and a third near Shiraz. Hundreds of direct attacks in the territories occupied by Israel, many of which hit Nevatim Air Base, Tel Nof Air Base, Hatzerim Air Base and Mossad Headquarters in Tel Aviv. Some sources suggest that one of the direct hits on Tel Nof Air Base with visible secondary explosions was actually the Arrow Battery with radar.

A man walks past a banner depicting missiles along a street in Tehran on April 19, 2024. Iran's state media reported explosions in the central province of Isfahan on April 19, while U.S. media cited officials as saying Israel had carried out retaliatory strikes against its archrival. This image broadcast by Iranian state television shows what is believed to be the city of Isfahan in the early hours of April 19, 2024, following reports of explosions heard in Iran's central province. © AFP - Iranian State TV (IRIB) - AFP · And this is where the source of concern for the region lies: until now it was believed that a form of “deterrence” between Iran and Israel prevented them from waging war directly, without going through Iran's “proxies” (such as Hezbollah). Remember that Israel has repeatedly carried out targeted eliminations of people linked to Tehran, or attacked Iran's interests either in Syria or Lebanon. But, in fact, this is the first time that it has launched an attack against Iranian territory with “vectors” such as drones or missiles. As before, on April 13, the Iranians attacked Israel directly on its territory for the first time.
