evidences: These are the diseases with which the driving license cannot be renewed in Spain in 2025 · The General Directorate of Traffic (DGT) has become more serious and strict and anyone who suffers from any of these 35 diseases will not be able to renew their driving license in 2025. The General Directorate of Traffic has just shared the new list of diseases that will prevent anyone who suffers from them from being able to get their driving license for the first time or renew their driving license from 2025. Some of these conditions may not seem very serious a priori, but the DGT considers them relevant enough to determine who can and cannot rehabilitate their driving license in Spain. What the General Directorate of Traffic is going to do is make the medical examination more strict, really assessing how serious the ailment is that the person interested in obtaining or renewing their driving license is suffering from, if of course they are suffering from it, to determine if they can really circulate on the streets and roads of Spain.

It is clear that the DGT has published a new list with 35 diseases that will prevent obtaining or renewing a driving license starting in 2025. The General Directorate of Traffic explains to VerificaRTVE that the diseases or physical conditions that may affect the renewal of the license "are listed in the Driver Regulations." This body clarifies that "this legislation is from 1997" and that "there has been no recent legislative change, nor is it expected that anything will be modified in this regard." The National Confederation of Driving Schools (CNAE) also explains to VerificaRTVE that "all diseases that make driving impossible or limit it are included in the Driver Regulations." The National Association of Driving Schools (ANAES) states along the same lines: "[The DGT] has not published any list of diseases that prevent driving and that generally affect drivers." Social media messages claim that the General Directorate of Traffic (DGT) has published a new list with 35 diseases that will prevent obtaining or renewing a driving license starting in 2025. It is false. There has been no new development or restriction in obtaining and renewing the driving license. The DGT explains to VerificaRTVE that "there has been no recent legislative change" and that restrictions linked to illnesses are listed in the Driver Regulations. A message shared more than 1,900 times on The publication attaches an image where we read "What diseases are included in the DGT list?" The snapshot lists pathologies such as celiac disease, diabetes, asthma, hyperthyroidism or anxiety, among others. Another publication shared more than 1,500 times spreads the same photograph with the message "the renewal of the driving license in Spain is complicated."

This is the list that the DGT has provided with the 35 diseases that could hinder or prevent the renewal of the driving license from 2025: One of the most important changes is the tightening of medical evaluations. Starting in 2025, drivers will have to undergo more rigorous medical examinations than before. The DGT has established an expanded list of diseases and conditions that can affect driving ability, and has defined stricter criteria for license renewal in these cases. Among the diseases that will be considered are cardiac, neurological, psychiatric, respiratory and metabolic diseases, such as diabetes mellitus. Drivers with these conditions will be required to submit detailed medical reports certifying that their illness is controlled and does not affect their ability to drive safely. In addition, these reports will be required to be issued by specialists in the corresponding areas.

The list of diseases with which the General Directorate of Traffic (DGT) will supposedly prohibit renewing the license, including some as common as celiac disease or anxiety, does not exist and has no basis. Despite the repeated information that is replicated on social networks, there is no change planned for 2025. The aforementioned list includes digestive conditions such as celiac disease or Crohn's disease, endocrine problems such as diabetes or parathyroid, as well as anxiety or cancer, according to the EFE agency in a note. But this list does not come from Traffic nor does it have a basis on which to stand: the psychophysical aptitudes required to obtain or renew a driving license have not changed since 1997, according to the DGT. Many publications maintain that Traffic will tighten next year the requirements for obtaining and renewing driving licenses for people with ailments that may put their driving ability at risk.

In these cases, it will be essential to have a medical report certifying that, despite the illness or treatment, the person is able to drive safely. The DGT has published a list of 35 diseases that could prevent the renewal of a driver's license. For this reason, starting in 2025, the DGT has decided to tighten the medical examinations necessary to renew the driving license. This means that drivers who suffer from certain illnesses or who are undergoing medical treatment that may compromise their driving ability, whether temporarily or permanently, could be denied the renewal of their license. For those who are being treated for or have any of these conditions, the key will be to maintain constant dialogue with their doctors and ensure that they have the necessary documentation to support their ability to continue driving. If not, they could face the harsh reality of not being able to renew their license in 2025.

On May 14, 2022, in Turin, the Ukrainian rap band Kalush Orchestra won the golden microphone of the Eurovision Song Contest. A year later, concerts around the world, collaborations with internationally renowned musicians and new songs keep the spirit of its members alive that night: the defense of their country and the support of their millions of compatriots. The Ukrainian Kalush Orchestra in the Eurovision 2022 final. | Getty Images ... The night of the grand final of Eurovision 2023 will begin with a performance by Kalush Orchestra, the brand new winners of Eurovision 2022 who are currently celebrating the anniversary of that magical night. On the stage of the Liverpool Arena, the Ukrainian band will present their performance Voices of a New Generation that includes Stefania, the song with which they achieved first place last year. After the triumph at the festival, Stefania became a symbol of the fight for freedom and a tribute to the Ukrainian resistance, although the truth is that the song was written by the leader of Kalush Orchestra, Oleh Psiuk, many years after the outbreak of the war in tribute to his mother. Regretting that the war with Russia has prevented the celebration of the festival in kyiv, the group has been very grateful to the United Kingdom for having taken up the baton as host: "We will perform for all Ukrainians to remind us that better days and the victory of our country are coming, as well as to show the world why Ukraine is fighting."

claim: They have put 200 immigrants from Mali in the school of a Galician municipality of 700 inhabitants. The school management has advised the girls' parents not to wear skirts, since the minors will have to live with them in the same facilities.
evidences: Galicia: the parents of the Mondariz-Balneario School (Pontevedra), they send me this video, they have put 200 immigrants from Mali in a municipality of 700 inhabitants. And be careful with this, the school management has advised the girls' parents not to wear skirts, since the minors will have to live with them in the same facilities.

A message shared more than 10,000 times on The text continues: "And beware of this, the school management has advised the girls' parents not to wear skirts, since the minors will have to live with them in the same facilities." This publication attaches a 6 minute and 50 second long video that shows a tour of the facilities of an educational center. In the recording you can see several people located in various rooms and clothing and footwear placed in some common areas. A female voice who introduces herself as the mother of a minor at the educational center explains that the migrants are using the school facilities. The video is from August and the migrants no longer live at the school. It is false that there are 200 immigrants staying in a public school in Mondariz and that the center's students have to "live with them" in the same facilities. As the mayor of the Mondariz-Balneario Council, César Gil, explains to us, the video that is now circulating on social networks "is from August" and was recorded by "a mother of a private school user" Marcote Mondariz. Gil assures that this mother "uploaded it to her social networks at that time" and adds that "now, a month later, it appears in other media." From the NGO ACCEM, in charge of protecting and caring for the migrants shown in the recording, they also point out to VerificaRTVE this video "dates back a month and does not reflect the current situation." Regarding the messages circulating on the Internet, the mayor of Mondariz-Balneario is blunt: "No, they currently live here in Mondariz, but they are in a hotel", known as Hotel Cemar. He clarifies that they arrived in the municipality on August 18 and, "as the hotel was full," what the private company that manages "the school, the hotel and a sports and nature complex" decided was to house them at the Marcote Balneario Bilingual School (42.2243377064878, -8.478670542691477). Gil explains that this was possible thanks to the fact that the educational center "is closed for holidays from mid-June, July and August." On this point, the NGO ACCEM insists that the school facilities "were temporarily enabled to serve as accommodation for a group of refugees from Mali." But they insist that "this transformation was seasonal and did not affect the regular operation of the school during the school period." César Gil assures that when the hotel stopped having the occupancy it had during the summer, "all the migrants began to be in the hotel facilities since August 31 and right now that is where they are." The management of the Marcote Balneario Bilingual School flatly denies that the migrants are housed in the center, adding that they do not live with the students and assure that they have not advised parents that the students not wear skirts. The center published a post reporting that classes for the 2024-2025 academic year began on September 11, more than a week after the migrants left this center. Therefore, it is false that the students of this center live or have lived with Malian migrants. On social networks they spread a video of a group of people in an educational center and claim that "they have put 200 illegal immigrants" in the Mondariz-Balneario school (Pontevedra) and that the students will have to live with them. It's false. The video circulating on the Internet is from August and was recorded at the Marcote Mondariz private school. The mayor of the municipality, César Gil, explains to VerificaRTVE that these migrants "do not live together or share any type of service with the students of the center" since since August 31 they have been staying at the CEMAR hotel. The NGO ACCEM, which is in charge of caring for these people, also assures us that this video "does not reflect the current situation."

More than 260 immigrants from Mali arrive in the municipality of Mondariz Balneario, the smallest in Galicia, in a school residence, which is also a hotel accommodation. This has caused parents to report that the school management has "advised the girls not to wear skirts, since the minors will have to live with them in the same facilities." Within the framework of the shelter agreed between the central government and the communities, all the immigrants have been installed in the Cemar Complex, where "they have all their needs covered" and where they are cared for by members of the NGO Accem. However, it is worth noting that the town barely has 700 inhabitants, that is, the 260 immigrants will represent a growth of just over 25% of the population. As explained by the town's mayor, César Gil, "no municipal services have been required for this group of refugees and the forecast is that they will remain in the municipality until December", although it is likely that many will leave earlier to join relatives settled in Europe, mainly in France. A Court of Becerreá (Lugo) has decreed the release of an immigrant, one of the immigrants hosted by the town, investigated for two crimes of sexual harassment and one of sexual assault without violence, two of the workers of the humanitarian organization that provides them assistance. According to judicial sources, regarding a complainant, the illegal immigrant is investigated for a crime of sexual assault and another of harassment. Regarding the other woman, she is being investigated as the alleged perpetrator of a crime of harassment. For their part, sources from the Department of Social Policy have detailed that the Board has implemented the protocol for psychologists to provide the necessary service to the two women. In addition, the Galician Administration will contact both workers, in accordance with the gender violence law, to whom they will offer the aid and programs intended for this purpose.

A Facebook post advertises that immigrants who have been in the United States for more than 3 months “meet” the requirements for food stamps, but this claim is false. Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) eligibility is not determined solely by how long a person resides in the country or their immigrant status, but applicants must primarily have limited income and resources. We corroborated this directly with a spokesperson for the government agency that administers this program. It is false that the immigrant who lives in the United States for more than 3 months already meets the necessary requirements for the approval of food stamps, as announced in a viral post spread on Facebook. We confirmed this directly with a USDA spokesperson, who stated that immigrants' eligibility is subject to meeting an income and resource limit, in addition to meeting the requirements required for immigrants. Although some immigrants can apply from “day 1” of their arrival in the country, while others require legal residence for at least 5 years, in both cases the income and resource requirements must be met to participate in the SNAP program. Among one of these requirements is that non-citizen immigrants must have lived in the United States for at least 5 years before being eligible for the program, the website provided by the spokesperson indicates.

Female unemployment, measured through women registered as unemployed in the SEPE offices, has been higher than that of men for more than two decades. In September it stood at 1,553,738 compared to 1,021,547 for men. Reviewing the historical series, male unemployment has had a more rapid decline, now falling below the level of September 2008, the year the financial crisis broke out. The female unemployment rate is even higher than that of that date, although the rate of reduction is equal to that of the male rate in 2024. One of the reasons why women's unemployment falls less is because more unemployed women register without having previously had a job. In September 2024, 4,011 more unemployment without previous employment were recorded than in August, while among men the increase is 2,360. In total, there are twice as many unemployed women with this characteristic as there are men, 161,392 compared to 79,646, respectively, and 40% of unemployed women without previous employment are over 44 years old. Furthermore, job creation among women has been greater in recent years, with female affiliation growing by 0.5% in September compared to August, in contrast to the decrease in male affiliation by 0.4%. This reinforces the thesis that the smaller decrease in female unemployment is due to the incorporation of more women into the labor market.

The specific figure must be set at the time of execution of the sentence, which the Xunta will do everything possible to ensure that it is "in the shortest possible time." The capture of a tweet attributed to the president of the Spanish government, Pedro Sánchez, which reads: "The self-employed quota will go from €288 to €433. We will not leave anyone behind", has been shared thousands of times on social networks since last February 23. However, the message is not authentic, it comes from a parody account about the president. According to the viral tweet, “the self-employed fee will go from €288 to €433.” To trace the origin of this supposed news, a Google search is done with the figures indicated in the tweet and with the keyword: “self-employed.” Among the first results is a news item published by the Spanish portal El Economista on February 22, one day before the publication of the parody account's tweet. In the article, the economist Javier Santacruz prepares some calculations taking into account as average “real income” the amount of 1,416.60 euros per month, which is 1.5 times the current minimum contribution base, the monthly self-employed contribution if contributions are based on real income would go from 288.99 euros to 433.48 euros. However, this increase is a hypothesis of Santacruz, but this variation had not been announced by the Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration, headed by José Luis Escrivá, at the date of publication of this verification.

In the period from January to June, employment has continued to decrease in each of the months. Since the economy fell into a depression in 2006, more than 240,000 jobs have been lost. After five consecutive years of declining employment, employment finally grew in 2012 and did so with an increase of 0.5%, which represents an increase of 5,000 jobs. Unemployment among those under 25 years of age has been reduced by 4,903 people (-14.9%) in the last twelve months, and by 11.8% compared to the previous month. Since the beginning of the legislature, the reduction in youth unemployment has been 6.3 points greater than that of general unemployment. As for the long-term unemployed, their unemployment rate has fallen by 11.7% in the last year (23,198 people), and 2.4% compared to November 2016. This reduction has been 3.4 points greater than that of general unemployment in this legislature. In 2016, unemployment has decreased in the Community in all sectors of activity: in Services (-8.9%; decrease of 30,158 people), in Construction (-18.5%; decrease of 9,190 people) and in Industry (-15.1%; decrease of 4,864 people). Unemployment also decreased by 499 people in Agriculture (-11.8%) and in the unemployed without previous employment (-8.9%), with 2,274 fewer unemployed.
